# PR #12719 retrospective

## Worked

Fresh exact-model sessions and equivalent neutral scope yielded independent tag findings. Source-only Sol work was sufficient; one Opus local-Git experiment exposed a compatibility condition beyond the PR's ordinary tests. Reviewer conclusions were not read or shared until both finals existed. Separate audit and synthesis addenda preserved independence and corrected claims without rewriting history.

## Deviations and remediation

- Coordinator metadata projection accidentally serialized entire owned agent records, exceeding the aggregate bound. Subsequent projections select explicit identity/status fields only. Initial history retained in PROCESS-DEVIATIONS.md.
- Opus's oversized policy/inventory responses are recorded in its final/addendum. Future output must count then page, never join hundreds of names or truncate line width. This rule was repeated in the synthesis dispatch.
- Namespace containment was mistaken for sufficient execution permission for some Git/product/interpreter writes. Per-target audit gaps and ungated substitutions are explicitly recorded, not repaired by a zero exit or a seal. Broad totals are excluded; public claims use pinned source plus individually retained command outcomes. Future fixtures must implement the actual callee guards before running or remain source-only. This correction was sent directly to the reviewer before closeout.
- Corrected the original tag fixture chronology through an addendum: remote B existed before add. The public sketch follows the actual fixture.
- The first reviewer reset attempted launch before Herdr's old occupant registration cleared. Owned-shell and agent-not-found reconciliation established readiness before a new UUID launch; no duplicate task was dispatched. Use explicit shell AND registration readiness before restart. Do not use a tight iteration budget as a substitute for lifecycle completion.

## Limits and tool notes

No observed review.py defect. A plain-directory snapshot mode for pinned API blobs is a potential feature, not a diagnosed bug. No UI or shared desktop resources used. Keep process lessons local to this assignment, not persistent agent memory. Review HTML remains unopened for outer batch presentation.
comment:
Two update edge cases remain at `4a0ef2e`: ordinary installs can stop following a changed remote default, and a tag accepted by `--branch` is not preserved by update.

**Verified:** The updater now follows an attached `dev` checkout to its newer commit instead of fetching the default branch and leaving it unchanged. Ordinary installs still update normally while the remote default retains the same branch name.

## Default installs stop following a renamed or changed remote default

The [new fetch path](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4a0ef2ea96f774ec63a6f542585dcbed2f00019c/bin/omarchy-plugin-update#L43-L58) uses the local branch name for every plugin, including installations made without `--branch`. Previously it fetched `origin HEAD`.

Local Git cases with fast-forwardable history:

| Upstream change after an ordinary install on `master` | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Rename `master` to `main`, then advance it | Updates to the new default | Fetch fails: `couldn't find remote ref master` |
| Switch default to newer `stable`, retain old `master` | Updates to the new default | Reports “up to date” while retaining the old content |

**Impact:** Existing ordinary installations can fail to update, or silently remain on an abandoned branch. The default case is unchanged only while the remote default keeps its original name.

**Suggested change:** Distinguish explicit branch selections from default-following installs. For example, record an explicit `--branch` choice when adding a plugin and use that recorded ref during updates, retaining `origin HEAD` for unmarked/default installs. This is a suggested design, not a tested patch. Following the initial branch for all installs is another possible policy, but it changes existing behavior and needs a recovery path when that branch disappears.

## A tag accepted by `--branch` is left behind on update

[Add passes the value directly to `git clone --branch`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4a0ef2ea96f774ec63a6f542585dcbed2f00019c/bin/omarchy-plugin-add#L138-L146), which accepts tags as well as branches. The resulting detached checkout reaches the updater's `branch="HEAD"` fallback.

Observed with a synthetic local repository:

```text
remote: tag v1.0 at A; default branch already at descendant B
add --branch v1.0  -> detached checkout at A
update --yes      -> fetch origin HEAD -> “Updated” -> checkout at B
```

**Impact:** A successful tag installation can move to the remote default's newer code on the next update rather than remain at the selected release. Detached-checkout update behavior predates this PR; the new add option makes it reachable through this command.

**Suggested change:** Reject tag/detached results if the option is branch-only, or explicitly preserve pinned checkouts during update. Do not silently substitute the remote default for the selected tag.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned base/head source and local-Git experiments using the real add/update scripts, with shell rescan and installed-plugin catalog stubbed. The comparisons above use retained individual command results and checkout contents. No stock suite, interactive shell integration, HTTPS/SSH transport or hosted-forge rename behavior was tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium initial inspection and synthesis; independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, followed by source/evidence adjudication and a fresh Astra Medium editorial check.
